title: Peer hostile-input crosswalk and IMAGE/WIPEOUT clip-vertex cap audit
mode: Primary-source research and local source audit; plan update only
scope: Refresh ACadSharp repeated-DXF stack-exhaustion and extended-data writer reports
Cross-check LibreDWG R2004 decompression allocation-capacity security evidence
Reconcile Autodesk WIPEOUT group-91/14/24 grammar with local parse, validation, and writer limits
Add an implementation-ready local cap-bypass item without adding test fixtures, dependencies, or a new top-level subplan

sources.name: ACadSharp issue #1281
sources.observed: Open report describes process-ending recursive stack growth for long DXF comment runs, repeated XDATA application blocks, and repeated IMAGE/WIPEOUT clipping count groups. The author supplies ASCII shapes and reports that shared reader paths affect Binary DXF. This was not reproduced here.

sources.name: ACadSharp issue #1282
sources.observed: Open report describes a DWG writer storing an individual application's EED byte length through signed 16-bit narrowing, corrupting payloads at 32,768 bytes and causing the object to disappear on read. This is a peer-writer report, not a local defect finding.

sources.name: LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS
sources.observed: The release notes describe CVE-2026-63474: per-section decoded logical-size changes could shrink a live R2004 decompression allocation while another cursor retained a larger logical stream. The local plan already tracks the distinct fixed-allocation/page-window protections.

sources.name: LibreDWG issue #1243
sources.observed: Historical report for the R2004 decompression heap-buffer-overflow later addressed by the 0.14.1 release note. Used only to trace the release evidence, not as evidence of a local issue.

sources.name: Autodesk WIPEOUT DXF entity reference
sources.observed: Documents group 91 as the number of following clip boundary vertices, repeated group 14/24 coordinates, two opposite corners for rectangular clipping, and at least three sequential vertices for polygonal clipping. It does not specify this project's implementation resource maximum.

sources.name: Local IMAGE/WIPEOUT source and hardening tests
sources.observed: DRW_Image::parseCode rejects declared group-91 counts above 100,000, but appends each group-14 coordinate without checking the cap. hasValidClipBoundary validates count agreement and shape without an upper bound. validatePayloadFields rejects more than 100,000 vertices on the writer path. processImage publishes without final clip-boundary validation; processWipeout validates shape but the no-declared-count state remains allowed. The existing repeated-record hardening test covers 20,000 ASCII comments, 20,000 XDATA pairs in ASCII/Binary, and repeated WIPEOUT group-91 counts in ASCII/Binary, but not over-cap group-14 vertices when group 91 is absent.

assessment.planImpact: Add PAR-135 (P2) under existing bounded-resource and 7BC/7BI payload work. Enforce the existing 100,000 clip-vertex ceiling at the shared DXF group-14 append site and add generated ASCII/Binary IMAGE/WIPEOUT max+1 cases with group 91 omitted. Keep validation local to the strict hardening target, selector, and owning CTest; no full suite, peer, or native gate is required.

method.webReview: Primary GitHub issue/release pages and Autodesk DXF entity documentation; no peer artifact execution
method.localReview: Read-only source inspection of DRW_Image parse/validation and dxfRW IMAGE/WIPEOUT dispatch, plus existing generated repeated-DXF hardening tests
validation: git diff --check -- DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md passed before receipt creation
Source locations cross-checked with rg and sed; no production or test source was edited
method.limitations: PAR-135 is source-confirmed but not runtime-reproduced in this research pass. The proposed guard preserves the current omitted-group-91 read tolerance within the implementation cap; whether that legacy form is semantically valid is deliberately left separate. Peer issue claims do not promote local or global support claims.
